lead: A memory bound read off `budget::live_bytes` alone can be vacuous; `allocated_bytes` is the counter that shows it.
body: A stream measured with its reused buffer already allocated peaks at tens of bytes at any row count, so a case asserting only "the peak stayed under a bound" passes identically when the drain never ran or the counters are not maintained; `budget`'s module doc names the distinction. Assert that the churn grows with the input while the live peak does not, two counters doing nothing cannot fake.
